BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Process note:** The Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" asks us to skip everything tagged [STANDARD] because it has supposedly been "reviewed and cleared by both sides." Nothing in the package supports that. Several [STANDARD] items conflict directly with our playbook, so I have reviewed the whole package. The label is the Seller's, not an agreed position.

## Part 1: Departures and Pushback

### A. Limitation package (highest priority)

**1. General cap (Cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m**
- The Seller's figure equals our **conditional fallback**, which is usable only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. No authority has been given.
- Our opening position is 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Pushback:** Reject 20%. Restate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal any movement toward the fallback without Amelia Frost's written approval.

**2. Thresholds (Cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, recoverable only above the basket**
- Our position is a de minimis of AUD 5k and a basket of AUD 50k, with the Seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.
- The Seller's version is a true deductible at 5x our figures, which would strip out a large share of realistic warranty claims.
- **Pushback:** Reject all three elements (de minimis, basket and excess-only recovery). Restate AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar.

**3. Time limits (Cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months; limitations apply to "all Claims"**
- Our general claims period is 24 months. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" wording is a hidden override. It would import the general regime into Title, Tax, IP and fraud claims, which our playbook prohibits.
- **Pushback:** Restate 24 months. Delete the "all Claims" sweep-up. Each category (general, Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant, fraud) keeps its own regime.

**4. Fundamental / Title (Seller's "simplicity" proposal)**
- The Seller proposes applying general caps and time limits to capacity and title warranties.
- Our position is a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. This is one of the most significant departures in the package. Title and capacity are not general warranties.

**5. Exclusive remedy / non-reliance / limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
- Our fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out is required across caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive it.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Insert the full carve-out and state that it cannot be waived.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**6. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)**
- Disclosure Letter 1.1 deems disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), and 1.2 adds the Accounts and public registers.
- Our position rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. Disclosure must be specific and fair.
- **Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2 and the reliance wording in Schedule 7. Require specific disclosure against identified warranties only.

**7. Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3)**
- The Seller would bar claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge of," including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
- Our position is to delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must name specific Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Pushback:** Delete 8.3. Given the DD findings below, this is critical: the Seller's clause would let it argue that we knew of every disclosed issue and therefore have no claim.

### C. Specific completion and transaction items

**8. Bluefen consent (Cl 3 / 6.3)**
- The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied** are in the data room.
- Our position requires effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are met **before Completion**. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent with satisfied conditions a condition precedent to Completion.

**9. Riverlark facility (Cl 2 / 7)**
- Approximately AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The Seller will provide a release **after Completion**. The Disclosure Letter (item 3) confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included.
- Our position requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is allowed only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Require a payout letter, repayment from the funds flow at Completion, and discharge documents in escrow or effective at Completion.

**10. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005)**
- DD-005 records AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are unquantified (item 5).
- Our position requires the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs to be either a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Pushback:** Require a specific line item or a price deduction for the bonuses and on-costs. Require the Seller to quantify the on-costs and confirm which conditions trigger payment.

**11. Ironquay IP (Cl 11.1)**
- The Seller limits the existing indemnity to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k per DD-010) and calls it "adequate." Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room (item 4).
- Our position is to broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k is not independently verified either way.
- **Pushback:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Broaden it to cover IP title and transfer, and preserve the SOW3 cure. Require a receipt or confirmatory assignment before Completion. Do not accept the AUD 180k figure as verified.

### D. Other open items

**12. Export / privacy incident (DD-006; Cl 4.6 / Sch 6)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The Disclosure Letter (item 6) says the file may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. It does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required.
- Our position: assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation, and do not concede that it is immaterial. Require preservation of logs, an investigation scope and timetable, and regular written updates. Recommend that the principal consider whether a specific indemnity is needed. I have not proposed an amount, consistent with the playbook.

**13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k; DD-008 and DD-011)**
- The Seller describes them as ordinary-course operating costs. The disclosure (item 8) does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Our position: assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence. Require the terms for each renewal (term, termination rights, pricing). Do not treat them as Debt or as a price deduction by default. The decision on whether they affect price should follow the assessment.

**14. Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime")**
- Our position: Tax and IP terms remain **open**. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Pushback:** Reject the folding of Tax and IP into the general regime. Keep them as separate categories with their own terms, which are still under negotiation.

**15. Title (DD-012 share register)**
- The Seller relies on its own share register. Our position: the register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Our own verification should cover this, including a search of the ASIC register and the Company's constitution. Confirm no security interests affect the shares, which also matters for the Riverlark release.

**16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- Neither item is in the Seller's update summary, but both are in the Disclosure Letter (items 7 and 9). The Seller says the lease notification and the Mossvale restriction do not, on the material shown, require consent to the share sale.
- The playbook does not cover these items specifically. **Pushback:** Do not accept the Seller's reading. Ask for the relevant clauses, confirm whether landlord notice or Mossvale consent is needed, and make those points a diligence request.

## Part 2: Recommendations Summary

1. **Treat the entire package as open.** Reject the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "already accepted" framing. Do not follow the efficiency note.
2. **Hold the playbook opening positions.** Reject the Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month period. Do not concede either without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
3. **Restate thresholds:** AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k basket, first-dollar recovery.
4. **Separate categories:** Title and capacity get their own regime (100% cap, six years, outside the basket and knowledge bar). Tax and IP stay open and separate. Delete the "all Claims" sweep-up.
5. **Insert the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, and state it cannot be waived.
6. **Reject general disclosure.** Delete the data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure and the Schedule 7 reliance.
7. **Delete the buyer-knowledge exclusion (Cl 8.3).**
8. **Completion conditions:** Bluefen consent with conditions satisfied before Completion; Riverlark payout and discharge at Completion; the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs as a funds-flow line or seller-funded.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the IP indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require a receipt or confirmatory assignment.
10. **DD-006:** preserve logs, require an investigation with updates, and reject the "not material" characterisation without assuming a breach either way.
11. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals on their terms, without automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction.
12. **Diligence follow-ups:** independent title and encumbrance evidence, the office lease and Mossvale consent position.

**Caveat:** This is a commercial-level review for the deal team. The drafting should be checked by NSW transaction counsel before it goes to the Seller, and any movement on the fallback positions requires Amelia Frost's written authority.
